headline: DNA is the code that builds and runs your entire body—3 billion letters of instructions
universal_truth: Information is the foundation of form; instructions precede construction
fun_facts: Your DNA contains about 3 billion base pairs—if printed, it would fill 200 telephone books
99.9% of human DNA is identical between all people; 0.1% creates all our differences
If all the DNA in your body were unwound and connected, it would stretch to the sun and back 600 times
discussion_questions: What does it mean that you're built from information?
How does 0.1% create such visible human diversity?
What 'instructions' are you passing on through your influence?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Inside nearly every cell in your body is a complete instruction manual for building you. Three billion letters, encoding everything from your eye color to how your neurons wire. This manual is DNA—and you carry it everywhere.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: DNA contains the instructions, but it's just a molecule—it can't read itself or build anything. How does information in DNA actually become a living, functioning body?
cliff.prompt: How does DNA information become a body?

options.text: DNA is transcribed to RNA, which is translated into proteins that do the actual work
options.response: Yes. DNA → RNA → Proteins. The genetic code is read and executed through this central process.

options.text: DNA directly controls each cell, telling it exactly what to do and when
options.response: DNA provides the blueprint, but proteins do the actual work...

q1.title: The Four Letters
q1.script: DNA uses only four chemical letters—A, T, G, and C. Three billion letters, arranged in specific sequences, spell out every gene. Different sequences create different proteins. The complexity of life emerges from just four characters.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Four Letters"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Almost Identical
q2.script: Humans are 99.9% genetically identical. The differences that create diversity—appearance, disease risk, personality tendencies—come from just 0.1% of our DNA. Small variations, enormous consequences.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Incredible Length
q3.script: Each cell contains about 6 feet of DNA, packed into a nucleus one millionth of an inch across. Your total DNA, from all cells, would stretch to the Sun and back 600 times. Information is incredibly dense.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Information precedes form. DNA teaches that complex outcomes begin as coded instructions. What patterns and information are you encoding—in habits, in relationships, in the minds you influence?
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 79. Tomorrow, we'll discover what blood does all day. Until then, marvel at the 3 billion letters that spell 'you.'
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Information Encoding - What Are You Writing?
growTrack.learning_objective: Consider what information you're encoding in others
growTrack.activity: DNA encodes instructions that persist. What 'instructions' are you encoding in others through your example, your words, your patterns? Consider one message you're consistently sending—intentionally or not. Is it what you want to transmit?
